reason: The historical value 3 is strongly corroborated, but the exact Greek domestic rule text governing 1993-94 has not been recovered. Cypriot domestic equivalence is source-supported and is modelled separately, so it is not used as a reason to guess the numeric quota.

sources.title: Bosman, Case C-415/93 - EUR-Lex
sources.finding: Records UEFA's 1991 3+2 framework, permitting national associations to limit first-division line-ups to three foreign players plus two assimilated players.
sources.scope: UEFA framework; not proof of Greece's exact domestic 1993-94 clause.

sources.title: Greek Law 1958/1991, Government Gazette A 122/5-5-1991
sources.finding: Official statutory framework for paid/professional sport and football bodies; it does not provide the recovered numerical foreign-player clause needed for 1993-94.
sources.scope: Primary Greek legal framework; numerical league rule still missing.

sources.title: Nikos Nioplias interview - AthleteStories
sources.finding: Nioplias recalls that each Greek club had only three foreign players in that era.
sources.scope: Strong historical corroboration, not a regulatory text.

sources.title: Novasports historical record - third foreign player, 30 November 1988
sources.finding: Records that on 30 November 1988 participation of a third foreign player was instituted in the Greek championship.
sources.scope: Established sports-media chronology; underlying signed federation/league decision or FEK not yet recovered.

sources.title: RSSSF - Foreign Players in Greece since 1959/60
sources.finding: Cypriots did not count as foreigners; some Albanian players with Greek roots also technically did not count.
sources.scope: Shows nationality != Greece cannot be used as the complete domestic eligibility rule.

domestic_equivalence.scope: Domestic Greek competitions only; continental competition nationality remains association-based.

implementation_blockers: Recover exact Greek federation/league or Government Gazette text that sets the numerical limit applicable in 1993-94.
